subject: DPA / SCCs: HelixMed transfer-impact addendum and order-form redline coordination
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixmed.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@helixmed.com, legal@helixmed.com
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: DPA & transfer impact questions (HelixMed)

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers look promising for our clinical search workload. Our legal and procurement teams began a parallel review and flagged a couple of items we need clarity on before we can proceed with the order form:

- We received a draft DPA but need explicit mapping to the new EU SCCs (controller/processor clauses). Can Redwood confirm which SCC template you rely on and whether Redwood will sign the updated Annex I/II mapping?
- Transfer impact: we need the completed TIA (transfer impact assessment) or an addendum confirming appropriate safeguards for transfers to US-hosted inference.
- Roles: HelixMed needs a short exhibit or table in the MSA stating controller v processor responsibilities for logging, backups, and customer data access.

I attached our internal TIA checklist (HelixMed_TIA_20270330.pdf) and the procurement team has an accelerated calendar — can we get a legal-side sync early next week?

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Procurement
HelixMed

Attachments: HelixMed_TIA_20270330.pdf (summary checklist)
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixmed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA & transfer impact questions (HelixMed)

Evan — thanks for sending the TIA checklist and the heads-up on timing. Looping in our legal lead Marissa and privacy engineer Karthik to run through your items. Quick notes up front:

- Redwood uses the European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor, 2021) and we maintain an internal Annex mapping for the most common deployment modes. We can provide the Annex + redline to the DPA.
- We already do a transfer risk assessment for US-hosted inference; happy to produce the TIA addendum you can attach to the MSA/order form.
- On roles: we agree an exhibit table is helpful. We'll propose wording for logging/backups/customer access that aligns to processor obligations.

Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm availability for a 30-min legal/technical sync on Mon (Mar 29) or Tue? We should aim to get a redlined DPA and an Order Form exhibit back to HelixMed by Tue EOD if possible.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixmed.com>, procurement@helixmed.com
Date: 2027-03-29T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial: DPA & transfer impact questions — proposed redlines

Sean / Karthik — following up with proposed redlines and questions for HelixMed. Attached: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (highlights in comments). High-level summary:

1) SCCs: We will attach the EU Commission SCCs (2021, controller-processor module) and propose to keep Redwood as Processor. However, HelixMed must retain Controller responsibilities around lawful basis and data subject rights coordination (we suggest language in Section 2.1 of the DPA).

2) Transfer Impact Addendum: We propose a short TIA addendum (two paragraphs) that references: (a) hosting region and transfer mechanisms; (b) organizational and technical safeguards (encryption in transit/rest, limited access, logging retention policy); and (c) sub-processor list + notice mechanism. Karthik — I put a stub in the doc, can you expand the safeguards language.

3) Roles Exhibit for MSA/Order Form: A simple table mapping (Controller: HelixMed — Data subject rights, retention schedule; Processor: Redwood — processing on behalf, encryption keys managed by Redwood unless customer KMS requested). HelixMed asked specifically about backups and log retention — we propose 90 days logs by default, 365 for paid retention add-on.

Questions / open items to confirm with HelixMed:
- Will HelixMed require Redwood to accept indemnity beyond what is in the MSA?
- Do they insist on HSM-backed KMS for keys in production (this changes order-form pricing)?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (redlines + inline comments)

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixmed.com>, procurement@helixmed.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-30T14:20:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA & transfer impact questions (technical answers + TIA addendum)

Evan — thanks for the checklist and the call earlier. Quick technical responses and the attachments I promised: the HelixMed_TIA_20270330.pdf you sent is on file (we referenced it) and we attached our draft TIA addendum as a paragraph in the redline doc (see section 4 of Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx). Key points:

- SCCs: Redwood will adopt the EC SCCs (controller-processor) and include an Annex I/II mapping in the DPA. We do not make substantive edits to the SCC core text but will fill Annex entries relevant to logging, subprocessors, and security measures.

- Technical safeguards (summary to include in TIA addendum):
  - Encryption: in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256).
  - Key management: default Redwood-managed KMS; HSM/KMS integration available for an add-on & procurement note.
  - Logging/Backups: access logs retained 90 days by default; backups held for 30 days for inference checkpoints; can extend per order form.
  - Subprocessors: canonical list updated monthly; 30-day notice for additions and stop-processing rights on material changes.

- Data subject requests: Redwood provides routing and support for requests; HelixMed remains Controller and must coordinate notices if we need to disclose data externally.

Action items:
- Sean: please propose a 30-min slot Tue Mar 30 10:00–12:00 CET for a legal + procurement call (I will join).
- Evan: please confirm whether HelixMed requires HSM-backed keys and whether they want longer log retention in scope for this order.

Karthik Iyer
Privacy Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference

2) We prefer 365-day log retention for access logs tied to audit/regulatory requirements.

We can take the proposed redlines and the TIA addendum as the baseline; procurement will expect a final DPA + Order Form exhibit for signature by EOD Wed Apr 6. Can we lock a call Tue Mar 30 11:00 CET to finalize the open items (HSM cost and indemnity language)?
